whereTheOverhangComesFrom.answer: rounding at the pixel grid, met by an engine box that starts at the raster's first column
steps: The region is rendered as asked, with no padding: docling_tesseract.py:128 makes the clip the region itself,
and :189 renders that clip. Nothing in the Python side or in the bridge widens it.
The scale is 0.814 px per pt because the region is 1720 pt tall and a raster side may be 1400 px (:132).
The region's left edge, 280 pt, falls at pixel 227.907. MuPDF renders whole pixels and takes the integer
bounds outward (floor of left and top, ceiling of right and bottom; the same bounds :140 preflights).
The raster therefore starts at pixel 227, which is 278.886 pt: 0.907 px, 1.114 pt, left of the region.
On the right it ends at pixel 782 (960.743 pt): 0.605 px, 0.743 pt beyond. Top and bottom land on whole
pixels (700 and 2100), so there is nothing beyond them.
Each of the three boxes starts at raster x = 0 exactly: the engine read ink in the first pixel column, which
is the column the region's left edge cuts. The mapping back to points (:244-249) is exact and unrounded,
so the box's left edge is the raster's left edge, 278.886 pt.

bound: The raster can pass the region by less than one rendered pixel on a side, so a true box
can too: under 1/scale pt. Here that is under 1.228571 pt. The contract's 1 pt is below it
whenever the scale is under 1 px per pt: any region over 1400 pt on a side, or over 1.6
million square pt. The smallest admitted scale (a 2000 x 2000 pt region) is about 0.632 px

whatStandsInTheWay: The 1 pt rule is in the contract file, which K9d does not own, and it is applied three times (the bridge, the
stored document result, fusion). A rule written only in document-ocr.ts cannot make the result accepted:
the contract refuses it on the next line, and again when the document result is stored.
The contract cannot compute one rendered pixel either: a published OCR result does not carry the render scale.
DocumentOcrBaseSchema is a strict object, so boxesBeyondRegion as a field of its own is a published change
(docs/api/openapi.json, the generated client). Issue codes are free strings up to 200 characters, so
OCR_BOX_OUTSIDE_REGION and a count written as an issue fit the published shape without a change.
